findings.evidence: Mathlib/GroupTheory/PresentedGroup.lean:129 `toGroup`, :151 `@[ext] theorem ext` are stated for `PresentedGroup rels`; the sibling `GroupPresentation.Group` (GroupPresentation.lean:200) is deliberately an `abbrev` for exactly this reason, and GroupPresentation.lean:92 documents that bodies here are sealed.
findings.fix: Re-export the universal property: `def lift (f : Fin (n-1) → G) (hcomm : ∀ i j, i.1+2 ≤ j.1 → f i * f j = f j * f i) (hbraid : ∀ i j, i.1+1 = j.1 → f i * f j * f i = f j * f i * f j) : BraidGroup n →* G`, with `@[simp] lift_sigma`, an `@[ext] hom_ext : (∀ i, φ (sigma i) = ψ (sigma i)) → φ = ψ`, and `closure_range_sigma : Subgroup.closure (Set.range sigma) = ⊤` (or an induction principle). Do not fix this with `@[expose]`.
findings.issue: `BraidGroup n` is a plain `def` in a non-`@[expose]` `public section`, so its body is sealed downstream. `PresentedGroup.toGroup`, `PresentedGroup.ext`, `induction_on`, `generated_by`, and `closure_range_of` are therefore all unreachable for `BraidGroup n`: no consumer can define a new homomorphism out of B_n (Burau, Temperley–Lieb, the roadmap's `burauAlexander`) or prove two homomorphisms out of B_n are equal. The whole file's own four homs were built inside the module, where the body is visible.

findings.evidence: Same convention as `mem_relatorSet_iff` (GroupPresentation.lean:176) and `mem_coxeterRelatorsOfList_iff` (Coxeter.lean:171), which exist precisely so consumers never unfold a sealed set.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem mem_artinRelations {r} : r ∈ artinRelations n ↔ ArtinRelation n r := Iff.rfl`.
findings.issue: `artinRelations n = {r | ArtinRelation n r}` also has a sealed body and no membership lemma, so a downstream user holding `ArtinRelation.comm i j h` cannot conclude `_ ∈ artinRelations n` (needed for `PresentedGroup.map`, or any relation-level reasoning).

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Ker.lean:364 `instance (priority := 100) normal_ker (f : G →* M) : f.ker.Normal` — matches `f.ker`, not the sealed alias.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem mem_pureBraidGroup {b} : b ∈ PureBraidGroup n ↔ permHom n b = 1` and `instance : (PureBraidGroup n).Normal`; rename to `pureBraidGroup` per the lowerCamelCase convention for data-valued defs.
findings.issue: `PureBraidGroup n := (permHom n).ker` is sealed, so `MonoidHom.normal_ker` does not apply to it downstream (`BraidGroup n ⧸ PureBraidGroup n` fails) and there is no membership characterization. The UpperCamelCase name also reads as a `Type`, not a `Subgroup`.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/GroupTheory/PresentedGroup.lean:49 `mk_surjective`, :97 `induction_on` — both stated for `PresentedGroup rels` and hence unusable through the sealed `BraidGroup`.
findings.fix: Add `theorem evalWord_surjective : Function.Surjective (evalWord (n := n))` (from `PresentedGroup.mk_surjective` and `FreeGroup.Quot.mk`), plus an `induction_on` for `BraidGroup n` stated over `evalWord`.
findings.issue: `evalWord` ships introduction lemmas only (`_nil`, `_cons`, `_append`); there is no elimination — nothing says every braid is `evalWord w`. Combined with the inaccessible `PresentedGroup.induction_on`, the combinatorial layer the roadmap builds on (`closes : BraidWord n → Diagram`) has no way to reduce a general element of `BraidGroup n` to a word.

findings.evidence: The only uses are `exponentSum` (155), `permHom` (222), `castSuccHom` (257) in this file; `grep -rn "permGen\|exponentSumGen\|castSuccGen" code/TauCeti` matches nothing else.
findings.issue: Six proof-only helpers are public with sealed bodies, so they are unusable but permanently part of the surface: `exponentSumGen` (144), `exponentSum_rel` (147), `permGen` (166), `permHom_rel` (171), `castSuccGen` (239), `castSucc_rel` (242). Each serves only the `PresentedGroup.toGroup` call two lines below it, and each hom's behaviour is already pinned by its `*_sigma` simp lemma.

findings.evidence: Line 101 `theorem comm (i j : Fin (n - 1)) (h : i.1 + 2 ≤ j.1) : sigma i * sigma j = sigma j * sigma i`, inside `namespace BraidGroup` (line 90).

findings.issue: `BraidGroup.comm` names the far-commutation relation but reads as "the braid group is commutative", which is false for n ≥ 3; under `open BraidGroup` it is a bare `comm`.

findings.evidence: `grep -rn "BraidWord" code/TauCeti` returns nothing; roadmap/TauCetiRoadmap/GeometricTopology/README.md:485 `def closes : BraidWord n → Diagram` and :490 `theorem alexander_eq_burau (β : BraidWord n)`.
findings.fix: Add `abbrev BraidWord (n : ℕ) := PresentationWord (Fin (n - 1))` and state `evalWord` over it, or drop the claim from the description.
findings.issue: The PR description advertises `BraidWord n` as a key definition, but no such declaration exists; the roadmap names `BraidWord n` as the type later stages consume.

summary: The braid group is a sealed-body `def` over `PresentedGroup` with no re-exported universal property, so downstream can neither build a homomorphism out of `BraidGroup n` (e.g. the Burau representation the roadmap needs) nor prove two such homomorphisms equal; the relation set, `evalWord`, and `PureBraidGroup` are likewise missing their characteristic lemmas, and six proof-only helpers are public.
